intended_object: Bookkeeping that takes the terminal state of the history problem restricted to [0, τ] and repackages it as an `InitialData` for the forward problem on [τ, T] (`D.tail`). This comes from the docstring and from the companion lemma `forwardInitial_eq`.
explanation: This is a gluing step internal to the library's argument in the Euler-equation development. It takes the terminal datum of the problem restricted to the history interval, `(B.initial τ …).terminalInitial (G.initial τ …)`. That datum consists of the coordinate path evaluated at time τ, its orbit smoothness and its zero angular mean. The definition copies its three fields into an `InitialData` structure indexed by the tail data `D.tail τ`, because the structure has to carry that index. Mathematically it is just "the state at time τ, used as the initial condition on [τ, T]". It is an auxiliary device for restarting the problem at time τ, not a standalone object from the literature. There is nothing to compare with Mathlib and no generality to assess.
